new_bank_questions.title: Exchangeable but dependent draws
new_bank_questions.body: A bag has one red and one blue ball. Draw both without replacement, marking red as 1. Give the probabilities of (1,0) and (0,1). Are the draws exchangeable? Are they independent?
new_bank_questions.answer: The two ordered outcomes each have probability 1/2, so permuting draw positions preserves the joint law: the pair is exchangeable. Each marginal probability of red is 1/2, but P(1,1)=0 rather than (1/2)(1/2)=1/4, so the draws are dependent. Their covariance is -1/4.

proofs_todo.title: Converse de Finetti representation for infinitely exchangeable Bernoulli sequences
proofs_todo.reason: The collapsed proof establishes that iid Bernoulli mixtures are exchangeable and gives a finite counterexample; it does not derive the converse via limiting empirical-frequency measures and uniqueness.
